title: Marketplace listing — copy experiments & integration requirements
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working artefact for two simultaneous goals: (1) run short copy experiments for the three primary cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP) to identify titles/taglines/descriptions that maximise CTR -> install requests; and (2) list the end-to-end technical and commercial integration requirements needed to get a Redwood hosted SaaS listing through each marketplace's review process.

Context and constraints (quick notes):
- Audience: platform/product-engineering, legal, finance (billing), and GTM ops. Keep copy length targets in mind for each marketplace UI.
- Tone: concise, developer-forward, production-first. Avoid marketing hyperbole. Emphasise reliability, latency SLAs, deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and cost predictability.
- Experiments should be instrumented to capture clicks, leads, and start-of-trial events.

Section A — Copy experiments (design + variants)
1) Experiment goals and metrics:
   - Primary: Marketplace page CTR -> Get started / Request trial conversion rate (7-day window).
   - Secondary: Demo requests, contact form submissions, and early provisioning success rate.
   - Quant: track impressions, clicks, installs/requests, and 1st API call success. Use UTM tags per variant.

2) Title / short headline (character guidance)
   - AWS: 60 char target; Azure: 80 char; GCP: 70 char.
   - Variant A (developer-first): "Redwood Inference — low-latency LLM inference API"
   - Variant B (cost-focused): "Scale LLM inference with predictable latency & cost"
   - Variant C (enterprise-ready): "SLA-backed LLM inference: hosted, dedicated, private"

3) Tagline / 1-liner (40-120 chars depending on marketplace slot)
   - Variant 1: "Run open and fine-tuned LLMs with predictable latency, autoscaling, and observability."
   - Variant 2: "Reduce per-token costs with caching, batching, and model routing policies."
   - Variant 3: "Full-stack inference for regulated workloads — VPC, KMS, and audit logs."

4) Long description (3 variants):
   - Dev-first variant (focus on DX): short bullets for API, SDKs, examples, and quickstart links. Include code snippet placeholder.
   - Ops variant (focus on reliability): emphasise SLAs, dedicated pools, fallback policies, and tracing/metrics.
   - Commercial variant (focus on procurement): highlight pricing models, marketplace billing compatibility, and private offers.

5) Feature bullets (pick 5 high-impact bullets for marketplace UI):
   - "Hosted API: text generation, embeddings, and chat with streaming and function calls."
   - "Dedicated Capacity: reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and burst options."
   - "Private Deployments: VPC & on-prem packages for regulated data and air-gapped infra."
   - "Observability: token-level cost/tracing and per-route dashboards for rollouts."
   - "Optimize: batching, quantization, and cache suggestions to lower unit costs."

6) CTA variants (A/B test these):
   - "Start free trial"  (default)
   - "Request dedicated trial"
   - "Contact sales for private deployment"

7) Asset checklist for copy publish (visuals + metadata):
   - 1 hero screenshot (dashboard listing with per-route latency graph)
   - 3 screenshots: API quickstart, Dedicated capacity config, Private deployment network diagram
   - Logo (SVG + PNG 512x512)
   - Short video (30–45s demo) optional for AWS/Azure.
   - Support contact email and link to pricing page (canonical URL)

8) Link tracking conventions (for instrumentation):
   - Add utm_source=marketplace, utm_medium={aws|azure|gcp}, utm_campaign=mp-listing-2025-11, utm_content=copyVariantX

Section B — Integration & listing requirements (technical + commercial checklist)
1) Marketplace-specific mechanicals (overview):
   - AWS Marketplace (SaaS): Must implement metering/billing integration (AWS SaaS Boost or Marketplace Metering Service). Validate private offers and consolidated billing flows. Ensure API for usage metering and pdf invoices mapping for finance.
   - Azure Marketplace (SaaS): Azure Marketplace requires publisher registration, MPN alignment, and SaaS Fulfillment API wiring. Must support Azure AD SSO for enterprise customers optionally.
   - GCP Marketplace (SaaS): GCP requires marketplace agreement, a billing connector, and often Cloud Marketplace Seller Portal onboarding. Provide Oauth2 or SSO integrations as necessary for provisioning.

2) Required technical endpoints & hooks:
   - Provisioning webhook: POST /marketplace/provision -> accepts marketplace payload, returns provisioningId.
   - Billing usage endpoint or meter: per-token or per-embedding event counter. Document expected batch frequency and idempotency rules.
   - Health and status endpoints: /healthz, /status with version, supported models list for runtime.
   - Entitlement check API: endpoint to validate customer entitlements and plan tier.
   - Deprovision webhook: handle unsubscribe events and data retention flags.

3) Security & compliance checklist (minimum asks):
   - SOC2 Type II report on file (or timeline if pending).
   - Encryption at rest and in transit; KMS integration for private deployments and marketplace private offers.
   - Data residency notes: which regions are supported for hosted metadata and customer data.
   - Pen test summary and vulnerability disclosure contact.

4) Legal / commercial artifacts to prepare:
   - Standard terms of service + marketplace partner addendum (one-pager).
   - Privacy notice mapping for marketplace registrants (consent flow).
   - Acceptable use policy, customer data handling (for E2E audits).

5) Operational readiness (SRE/Support):
   - On-call rotation for first 30 days after launch with runbook for marketplace incidents.
   - SLAs and escalation playbook for provisioning failures.
   - Playbook to fallback customers to an alternate region or model variant if capacity constrained.

6) Acceptance test plan (must pass before submit):
   - End-to-end provisioning test (simulate marketplace webhook, confirm account creation, entitlement assignment).
   - Billing test (simulate usage events and verify marketplace reporting and billing reconciliation).
   - SSO test (if SSO option enabled): confirm SAML/OAuth flows complete and user mapping created).
   - Security test: automated scan baseline and a manual review of auth flows.

7) Release artifacts for submission packet (what marketplace review expects):
   - High-res logo and marketing screenshots.
   - Seller contact info, support SLA, and training docs for cloud reviewers.
   - Technical contact for integration questions and a sandbox account for reviewers.
   - Billing configuration documentation and sample invoices.

Section C — Risk matrix & edge cases (working notes)
- Private offers: some customers will ask for contract terms outside marketplace billing; prepare standard private-offer templates and clear instructions on settlement outside marketplace.
- Metering granularity: marketplaces often expect coarse-grained metering (monthly seats/units). Map Redwood's per-token metering to a marketplace-compatible unit (e.g., 1 unit = 10k tokens) and document conversion math.
- Availability windows: dedicated customers may require fixed maintenance windows. Ensure UI metadata supports maintenance scheduling.

Section D — Quick launch timeline proposal (high-level)
- Week 0–1: finalize copy variants, image assets, and tracking tags.
- Week 2: implement marketplace hooks in staging + automated tests.
- Week 3: run internal acceptance tests and security scans.
- Week 4: submit to marketplace review (AWS/Azure/GCP submissions staggered to reduce review load).
- Week 6: expected earliest approval (dependent on review back-and-forth).

Open questions / decisions to make (notes-to-self):
- Which marketplace do we prioritise for a private-offer-first launch? Suggest: AWS (largest enterprise buyer base) then Azure.
- Do we ship per-token metering out of the gate or map to a monthly unit? (Finance needs decision by Week 1).
- Who is the technical reviewer for marketplace sandbox credentials? (Assign owner).

References and related docs:
- Confluence: marketplace-onboarding (linked above).
- Jira: ENG-1298 (integration epic), FIN-540 (billing mapping).

Next steps (actionable):
- [Priya] Finalise 3 copy variants and send to creatives for screenshots (due +3 days).
- [Ethan] Standup staging endpoints for provisioning and billing (due +7 days).
- [Mariana] Draft the marketplace TOS addendum and privacy mapping (due +10 days).
- [Samir] Coordinate test accounts with AWS Marketplace enablement contact (due +5 days).

Notes (informal):
- Keep copy technical and specific; too many buzzwords reduce conversion with developer buyers.
- Use customer language from existing case studies where possible (latency numbers, cost savings percentiles).
- Iterate quickly — marketplaces respond faster to clear, minimal feature submissions than to overloaded listings.
